tool.name: dDocent Remake Reference
tool.description: re-assemble the reference from trimmed reads with new assembly parameters
tool.command:
mkdir -p work && cd work &&
## remake_reference.sh discovers its input by filename (Locality_Individual.F/R.fq.gz) #for $element in $reads ln -s '$element.forward' '${element.element_identifier}.F.fq.gz' && ln -s '$element.reverse' '${element.element_identifier}.R.fq.gz' && #end for
## the sample names end up in unquoted shell loops and in namelist, so keep them plain for f in *.F.fq.gz; do case "\$f" in *[[:space:]/]*) echo "ERROR: collection element '\$f' contains whitespace or a slash; dDocent cannot use it as a file name." >&2; exit 1 ;; esac; done &&
## remake_reference.sh takes K1, K2, similarity, assembly type and processors ## positionally and never asks for them when all five are given remake_reference.sh '$assembly.k1' '$assembly.k2' '$assembly.sim' '$assembly.atype' \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} < /dev/null &&
## the script reports the contigs it assembled but exits 0 even when the assembly ## was aborted early, so the output is checked explicitly test -s reference.fasta || { echo "ERROR: remake_reference.sh did not produce an assembly - reference.fasta is missing or empty." >&2; exit 1; }

param.name: reads
param.label: Trimmed reads
param.help: The trimmed reads collection of the dDocent pipeline, i.e. the reads that were assembled into the current reference. The element identifiers must be the sample names used by dDocent (e.g. PopA_01).

param.label: Assembly type
param.help: Must be the layout the reads were trimmed for. Single-end data sets cannot be re-assembled with this tool, because the input is a paired collection; run the dDocent pipeline again instead.
param.option: HYB - a mixture of overlapping and non-overlapping paired-end fragments

tool.help:
What it does ------------
``remake_reference.sh`` re-runs only the reference assembly step of dDocent on reads that are already trimmed. It is the cheap way to explore the assembly parameters: the assembly takes seconds to minutes instead of re-running the trimming step, and it needs no mapping and no SNP calling.
The tool therefore takes the *trimmed reads* collection of a completed dDocent pipeline tool run, so a new (K1, K2, similarity) combination can be tried without touching the raw data, and returns a new ``reference.fasta`` that can be fed back into the pipeline as a reference from the history.
Parameters ----------
K1 Minimum number of times a read must be seen *within one individual* to be used for the assembly; higher values remove more sequencing errors.
K2 Minimum number of *individuals* a read must be seen in; higher values keep only reads that are shared across the sample set, which removes individual-specific errors and low-level contamination.
Similarity CD-HIT threshold used to collapse the assembled sequences into contigs. dDocent recommends 0.9; because the assembly clusters forward reads only, the effective threshold used by CD-HIT is ``max(similarity - 0.1, 0.8)``.
Assembly type Must match the layout of the reads: PE for standard ddRAD fragments, RPE for randomly sheared paired-end libraries, OL for paired-end libraries whose fragments are shorter than twice the read length and HYB for a mixture of overlapping and non-overlapping fragments. OL and HYB merge overlapping read pairs with PEAR first, so they are noticeably slower.
Choosing the parameters -----------------------
dDocent ships two survey scripts (``ReferenceOpt.sh`` and ``RefMapOpt.sh``) that sweep K1, K2 and the similarity and evaluate the resulting assembly. They need a compute budget of days and a human to read the plots, so they are not wrapped here; the recommended procedure in Galaxy is to run this tool for the handful of parameter combinations that the survey on a subset of the data suggests.
